gartner-hype-cycle-1999-010.note: Opened Wikipedia Jini: introduced July 1998, moved to Apache as River 2007, last release Oct 2016, retired 2022; no adoption figures. No evidence of 5% use; D16 gives miss at P=2004 (abandoned 2007 <= P+5).

gartner-hype-cycle-1999-011.note: providersedge.com PDF returns a captcha page; same report opened at devbiz.narod.ru/home/kozloff/DMS/KPMG_KM_2000.pdf: 423 organisations with turnover above GBP 200m, 38% had a KM programme in place (fielded 1999). Mainstream by 1999-2000 <= P+2=2006: hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-1999-012.note: Wikipedia XML confirms W3C Recommendation 10 Feb 1998 but gives no adoption share; the slideshare page cited for Yankee Group 2004 (48% deployed XML web services) is dead (resource load error). Mainstream-by-2003 rests on the builders' estimate, but XML in routine enterprise interchange by 2003 is not seriously in doubt; hit at P=2001 kept.

gartner-hype-cycle-1999-014.note: Opened Wikipedia DigiCash (5,000 users, 300 merchants by 1998; Chapter 11 1998; assets sold 2002) and Ecash (Mark Twain Bank trial 1995-1998, 5,000 customers; does not mention CyberCash, so builder B's CyberCash 2001 line is unsourced). Never 5%: miss at P=2009.

gartner-hype-cycle-1999-015.note: Opened Wikipedia VRML ('never seen much serious widespread use', mainly education/research) and Web3D (plug-ins slowed adoption; WebGL 1.0 March 2011). No adoption figures, but nothing suggests 5% of users; miss at P=2004.

gartner-hype-cycle-1999-016.note: Google blog and PR Newswire (Oct 2014): Northstar survey of 1,400 US smartphone users, 41% of adults use voice search daily, so roughly a quarter of all adults in 2014; Pew 2017 page returns 403. Mainstream 2014 = P+5 for P=2009: partial (no evidence of 20% by 2011).

gartner-hype-cycle-1999-017.note: Wikipedia EMV: Carte Bancaire chip deployed in France from 1986, chip cards credited with cutting fraud since 1992; UK chip and PIN 14 Feb 2006; 70% of US consumers had EMV cards April 2016. France mainstream before 1999, so hit at P=2004 under the one-major-market test.

gartner-hype-cycle-1999-018.note: Pew fact sheet confirms US home broadband 6-9% (2001), 15-19% (2003), 23-26% (2004), so US-only gives mainstream 2004 = P+3. But StatCan The Daily 23 Sep 2003: 2.8 million Canadian households had broadband in 2001 (about 24% of ~11.6M households), and builder B itself notes Korea passed 20% around 2001; under the one-major-market test both builders used for Smart Cards, mainstream by P=2001: hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2000-004.note: Wikipedia Tablet computer: Microsoft Tablet PC pen devices 'failed' on pricing and usability; pens are optional accessories, no share figures. Wikipedia Apple Pencil: launched 2015, standard iPad support only from 2018. No evidence of 5% of new devices by P=2010 or 50% by 2015: miss.

gartner-hype-cycle-2001-001.note: Toshiba PR (22 Oct 2009) and phys.org: Dynario limited to 3,000 units, Japan-only direct orders, as a market test. Electronic Design article is dated Feb 2004 and says commercial products had yet to emerge (not that vendors missed targets, as builder B states). Never 5%: miss at P=2011.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-017.note: Builders' BPTrends PDF returns a captcha page and Wikipedia BPM gives no share. New source opened: InformationWeek 'The Secret Sauce of BPM Success' cites Forrester (Sept 2007, 400+ North American and European tech decision makers): about 60% of organisations already using a BPMS, 19% more planning to. Mainstream by 2007 <= P+2=2012: hit is supported (pass 1 contest lifted).

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-018.note: Wikipedia Windows Search: MSN Desktop Search 13 Dec 2004; integrated in Windows Vista released 30 Jan 2007 and every later Windows. With Windows on most new PCs, 50% of new units by 2007-2008, within P+2=2009: hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-019.note: Wikipedia Linux adoption: about 1% worldwide desktop in 2008, 4% Feb 2024, 5% June 2025; India 16.21% July 2024. Below 5% through P+5=2015 in any major market: miss at P=2010.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-020.note: Toshiba PR (22 Oct 2009) and phys.org: Dynario 3,000 units, Japan-only market test; Electronic Design (Feb 2004) says commercial products had yet to emerge. Never 5%; miss at P=2015.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-025.note: Wikipedia WiMAX: peak of just over 20 million subscribers worldwide (Aug 2011), Korea 350,000 by end 2008, Yota to LTE May 2010, Sprint dropped WiMAX devices CES 2012. Far below 5% of broadband in any major market: miss at P=2010.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-026.note: Pew 'Wikipedia, past and present' (2011) and phys.org: 36% of US internet users (25% of all adults) used Wikipedia in Feb 2007, 53% in May 2010. Mainstream by 2007 under the consumer reading, before P=2010: hit. The ericbrown.com page gives no wiki percentage, so the enterprise reading stays unevidenced, but it does not change the verdict.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-027.note: oled-info (Omdia): OLED 53% / AMOLED 51% of smartphone displays in 2024, first time above LCD; 57% Q1 2024, 63% Q1 2025 (Counterpoint page shows no figures). Electronics Weekly (IHS iSuppli, May 2011): 49.4M AMOLED units shipped in 2010, mainly phones, against roughly 300M smartphones, so at least 5% by P=2010 with mainstream in 2024: partial.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-030.note: Wikipedia TPM: TPM laptops from 2006; all new Microsoft device models implement and enable TPM 2.0 since 28 July 2016; Windows 11 requires it. Dark Reading page returns 403, so the 100M-in-2007 figure is unchecked. 50% of new PCs by 2016-2017 is within P+2=2017: hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-031.note: Avasant (2006 survey, ~200 IT executives): 19% had SOA deployed, 11% piloting. GovTech on Gartner 2008: 53% of respondents already using SOA, near-universal in Europe. Mainstream by 2007-2008, before P=2010: hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-033.note: Wikipedia Microsoft Tablet PC: first devices 2003 at US$2,000+, stylus reliance kept them from displacing laptops; no share figures; superseded by UMPC, Slate PC and Surface (2012). No evidence of 5% of notebooks by P=2010: miss either way on the abandonment flag.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-034.note: Wikipedia XBRL: FDIC an early user (no mandate date given); SEC taxonomy deployed from 2008 in phases, largest filers first; HMRC and Companies House iXBRL 2011; EU ESEF 2021. US public filers fully covered by 2011, within P+2=2012: hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-035.note: Accenture 'A new era for RFID in retail' PDF, Figure 1: North American retailers 2018 = 92% overall (46% piloting, 18% implementing, 28% full adoption), 2020 = 93% (47% full); 34% overall in 2014. First evidenced 20% full adoption is 2018 = P+3, with 5% well before P=2015: partial. Loss Prevention Media gives 93% overall only; Wikipedia RFID not needed.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-036.note: Pew 'Video Calling and Video Chat' (Oct 2010): 20% of US internet users had made online video calls in April 2009, 23% in 2010. Mainstream 2009 under the internet-user test, before P=2010: hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-039.note: Pew Location-Based Services (Sept 2013): 74% of adult smartphone owners get location-based directions or info; Pew Mobile fact sheet: smartphone ownership 35% (2011), 39-46% (2012). About 30% of adults by 2012 (74% x ~45%), so mainstream within P+2=2012: hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-040.note: Wikipedia Business rules engine (the only builder source) says engines date from the early 1990s and were typically used in finance and insurance, with no adoption share; one audit search found only the 2008 Forrester Wave, no adoption survey. Hit needs 20% of the relevant industry in production by P+2=2009; the 2007/2008 mainstream year is a judgement with no evidence, so pass 1's contest stands.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-041.note: Opened FCC Local Telephone Competition (Dec 2010, DOC-310264A1): residential interconnected VoIP 19.2M of 91.5M residential voice connections in Dec 2008 (21%), 27.1M of 87.1M in Dec 2010 (31%). Computer Weekly (2007): hybrid IP PBX 63% of PBX/KTS line shipments Q1 2007. Mainstream by 2008 at latest, within P+2=2009: hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-042.note: Opened Wikipedia 'Speech synthesis': Narrator with Microsoft Sam 'shipped with all Windows 2000 operating systems, and subsequent Windows XP systems'; VoiceOver in Mac OS X 2005. TTS was a default feature on well over 50% of new PCs before P=2007, so under the D16 device-feature test it was mainstream at the placed year; the builders' handset test is not the dominant 2005 reading and is the only one giving a miss. Hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-043.note: Opened Call Centre Helper 'IVR usage is still widespread' (ContactBabel UK 2009 guide): speech recognition in 8% of contact centres in 2004 and 8% in 2009, so at least 5% by P=2007; 'Contact centres hang up on speech recognition' (ContactBabel, Feb 2012): 10% average (23% large), below 20% at P+5=2012. Partial, now on measured data rather than an estimate.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-044.note: Opened ECIN (2003): the META Group timing the builders cite is a forecast, with no adoption figure, so it does not itself support the years. A 2005 survey of 403 US IT professionals (64% used web services to integrate internal applications; ResearchGate 'Web services: the third wave', page 403, figure seen in search result) supports mainstream by 2005, before P=2007. Hit, on thinner evidence than claimed.

gartner-hype-cycle-2007-012.note: Opened Wikipedia 'Wii': launched 19 Nov 2006, 101.63M units, Wii Remote uses a MEMS accelerometer and IR for gesture/motion input. No US series on the page, but tens of millions of US units plus Kinect (2010) put gesture-input devices in over 20% of US households well before P+2=2019 under the motion-controller reading both builders used. Hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2007-013.note: Opened Wikipedia 'Mashup (web application hybrid)' (definition only, no adoption figures) and 'Yahoo! Pipes' (Feb 2007 to 30 Sep 2015; Google Mashup Editor ended 2009). The pages define mashup as a web app combining sources via APIs, a practice both builders say became routine by about 2010 (hit), while their 'distinct tool category' test gives a miss; no measurement backs either reading, so the miss is not supported.

gartner-hype-cycle-2007-014.note: Opened Wikipedia 'Second Life' (peak 88,200 concurrent Q1 2009; about 1M regular users 2013; 800-900k end 2017) and TIME (2021: about 750k MAU, brand storefronts abandoned). Far below 5% of internet users by P+5=2022 under the dominant 2007 Second Life reading. Pew 2008 page returned 403. Roblox-style game platforms would need a broader reading. Miss.

gartner-hype-cycle-2008-020.note: Opened Wikipedia 'Innovation management': idea management named as a common tool, no adoption figures; builders' only evidence. One targeted search found only vendor and market-size reports, no organisational adoption share. The partial rests on an estimated year_5pct of 2010 with no measurement; neither 5% by 2013 nor below 5% is supported.

gartner-hype-cycle-2008-022.note: Opened Pew 'Wikipedia, past and present' (Jan 2011) and Phys.org: Wikipedia used by 36% of US internet users (25% of all adults) in Feb 2007 and 53% (42% of adults) in May 2010, above 20% before P=2013. Builder B's enterprise source (ericbrown.com) gives no wiki percentage, so the enterprise reading is unmeasured, but the hit holds on the public-wiki reading. Hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2008-023.note: Opened Pew 'E-Reading Rises as Device Ownership Jumps' (Jan 2014): e-reader ownership 24% of US adults in Sept 2013 and 32% in Jan 2014; Pew 'Technology Device Ownership 2015': 19% in 2015. The e-paper device proxy passed 20% in 2013, at P=2013 (some LCD Kindle/Nook models inflate it slightly). Hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2008-024.note: Opened Wikipedia 'Microsoft Tablet PC': first devices 2003 at US$2,000+, price and stylus reliance 'kept them from displacing laptops before Apple's iPad'; Microsoft moved to Surface in 2012. No source puts pen Tablet PCs anywhere near 50% of notebooks, and any 5% share of later convertibles came after P=2013, which the rule cannot credit. Miss under the dominant 2008 (Microsoft-spec) reading.

gartner-hype-cycle-2008-025.note: Opened Avasant 'SOA Adoption Trends' (2006 survey, about 200 IT executives): 19% had SOA in place, 11% piloting; Government Technology (2008, Gartner survey): 53% of organisations already using SOA. Mainstream (20%+) by about 2007-2008, before P=2013. Hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2008-026.note: Opened Pew 'Location-Based Services' (Sept 2013): 74% of adult smartphone owners use location-based directions or information; Pew Mobile Fact Sheet: smartphone ownership 35% (2011), 51-58% (2013). About 40% of US adults by 2013, within P+2=2015. Hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2008-027.note: Opened Wikipedia 'SOAP' (1.1 Note 2000, 1.2 Recommendation 2003; REST later dominant, no adoption figures) and ECIN (META Group forecast, not a measurement). The measured support is the 2005 survey of 403 US IT professionals (64% used web services for internal integration; ResearchGate page 403, figure from search result), so mainstream by 2005, before P=2010. Hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2009-002.note: Opened Wikipedia '3D television': DisplaySearch shipments 2.26M (2010), 24.14M (2011), 41.45M (2012), against roughly 240M TVs a year (10-17%); production ended 2016 and Sony and LG dropped 3D in January 2017. Never 50% of new units and abandoned before P+5=2024. Miss.

gartner-hype-cycle-2009-004.note: Gartner glossary page for CoDA returned 403 (Cloudflare) and the Wayback copy is blocked by egress; Wikipedia 'Context awareness' (builder B) has no mention of CoDA or adoption data. CoDA was an analyst-defined pattern with no product category or measured uptake, later relabelled 'context-enriched services'; nothing supports 5% of organisations by P+5=2024. Miss, on absence of evidence.

gartner-hype-cycle-2009-005.note: Opened TechCrunch (Dec 2008, comScore): YouTube handled 2.73bn US searches in Nov 2008, 25.4% of Google-site searches, more than Yahoo; Pew 'State of Online Video' (June 2010): 69% of US internet users watched or downloaded online video in 2009. Video search was mass behaviour by 2008-2009, before P=2019. Hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2010-030.note: Same pages as 2007-014: Wikipedia 'Second Life' (about 1M regular users 2013, 800-900k 2017) and TIME 2021 (about 750k MAU). Public Second Life-style social worlds stayed far below 5% of internet users through P+5=2025; game platforms (Roblox) are a different reading. Miss.

gartner-hype-cycle-2013-004.note: Opened Pew short read (9 Jan 2020; survey June 2019, n=4,272): 21% of US adults regularly wear a smartwatch or fitness tracker. Mainstream in 2019, within P+2=2020. Hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2014-040.note: Builders cite only Wikipedia (SAP HANA page opened: release Nov 2010, S/4HANA 2015, no adoption figures). Opened RTInsights 'Why the Move to In-Memory Technology?' (16 May 2016, 303 data professionals, Redis Labs-linked): 28% of organisations employ in-memory technologies, 23% piloting. Skewed sample and broader than BI, but with in-memory engines default in Power BI/Qlik/Tableau it supports 20% by P+2=2018. Hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2014-041.note: Opened Wikipedia 'Activity stream' (News Feed Sept 2006; activity streams built into Jive, Yammer, Chatter, no figures), 'Yammer' (1M users 2010, 4M 2011, Microsoft 2012) and 'Microsoft Teams' (launched March 2017, activity feed; 20M DAU Nov 2019, 75M Apr 2020, 250M MAU July 2021). No organisational survey, but feed-based suites bundled in Office 365 make 20% routine use by P+2=2021 well supported; both builders' mainstream years (2013, 2017) fall inside the window. Hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2014-042.note: Downloaded the PwC/Manufacturing Institute PDF (NIST-hosted, 2014): 24.6% of US manufacturers use 3D printing for prototyping only, 9.6% prototyping and production, 0.9% final products only, so about 35% routine use in 2014, before P=2019. Eurostat's 4% covers all enterprises, a broader population than the reading. Hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2014-045.note: Opened Google blog (Oct 2014, Northstar): 41% of US adult smartphone users talk to their phones every day (the PR Newswire release gives teen figures only); with smartphone ownership at 51-58% in 2013 (Pew) that is above 20% of adults. Pew short read (Dec 2017): 46% of US adults use voice assistants. Mainstream by 2014-2017, within P+2=2018. Hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2016-026.note: Opened O'Reilly 'AI adoption in the enterprise 2020' (1,388 respondents, tech-skewed): 27% mature (production) AI/ML in 2019, over half in 2020. McKinsey survey pages returned 503 (WebFetch and curl). Even discounting sample skew, 20% in production by P+2=2023 is supported. Hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2016-031.note: Opened Pew short read (Dec 2017): 46% of US adults use digital voice assistants (42% on smartphones), which answer spoken questions; Wikipedia 'Virtual assistant': Siri Oct 2011, about 1bn frequent assistant users worldwide by mid-2017. Mainstream by 2017, before P=2021; an enterprise Watson reading would also be met by LLM assistants before 2023. Hit.
